verdicts.note: Chief deputy coroner running to 'build upon this solid foundation' (S1); never held elected office (S1), so -1 not -2.

'Maintain a balanced budget while minimizing the use of taxpayer funds' through in-house strategies (S1) is an explicit restraint statement. The federal grant funding he also cites (S1) is outside revenue, not a call for more local spending.

Low is the right confidence. His community education initiative serves 'public awareness, public safety, and prevention to avoidable deaths' (S1), and he wants to bolster it (S2). That leans toward prevention but is not set against enforcement, and a coroner only loosely engages the safety axis (policing, prosecution, treatment). Low keeps it out of alignment math.

Direction holds: she will 'bring prevention and education to the forefront' on fentanyl deaths, suicide and mental health (S1, S2). But the safety axis is enforcement versus prevention/treatment in public-safety policy, and a coroner's public-health education program does not trade off against enforcement. Her own statement names the coroner's duty as including 'to prosecute the guilty' (S1) and lists DOJ hidden-homicide training (S1). Mapping her stance onto the axis is an inference, which the guide defines as low. Low also matches the confidence given to Waldrop's similar prevention-education evidence, so the two are treated alike.

Former Stevens deputy coroner now with the Spokane County ME, outside current office leadership, promising more transparency and a budget shift to autopsies (S1, S2). +1 medium fits an experienced challenger running on change.
